decision_rule: Bind the eleven ranked reported-length claims to a source-passage assessment. This checks quoted number and stated scope only. It does not verify a common current axis or set individual scientific claim review status.

entries.editorial_note: The introduction reports an approximate circumpolar length. It does not trace a reference contour or current core; NASA's separate 21,000 km approximation remains a distinct variant.
The introduction reports a Pacific eastward subsurface pathway scale. It is not a measured instantaneous streamline and does not include Atlantic or Indian undercurrents.
The source describes a broad Humboldt Current belt; its separate approximately 1,000 km Peru study area must not be substituted for this system extent.
The paper investigates a continuous austral-winter shelf-edge flow involving the Leeuwin, South Australian, and Zeehan currents. The number is seasonal and compound, not the Leeuwin Current alone.

The PICES ocean review reports a 3,000 km extent for the broader California Current System from Baja California Sur to northern Vancouver Island. Its same page distinguishes that system from the California Current proper. This is a regional system extent, not a measured current-core axis; retain the number only under system scope.

The 2015 observational oceanography article describes a roughly 3,000 km Kuroshio journey from about 12°N to 35°N. That introductory geographic estimate is not a traced whole-current axis; the Kuroshio Extension remains a separate continuation.

Tomczak and Godfrey report about 2,500 km for the Gulf Stream proper as a free jet downstream of Cape Hatteras toward the Newfoundland Rise/Grand Banks. This excludes the Florida Current and downstream North Atlantic Current. The textbook does not present a measured reference streamline.

Tomczak and Godfrey report about 1,200 km downstream from the Florida Straits to shelf separation near Cape Hatteras. This is the Florida Current segment, not the full Gulf Stream System, and is not a traced reference streamline.

The accepted-manuscript abstract reports approximately 1,700 km from Seward to Samalga Pass. This is a source-defined northern Gulf of Alaska/eastern Aleutian coastal system, separate from the offshore Alaska Current. Intermittent 1984-2014 observations support the paper context; the number is not a measured simultaneous streamline or every coastal flow sharing this name.

Section 1.1 reports an upper-continental-slope system span; the Figure 2 caption and subsequent discussion limit circumpolar continuity at the Antarctic Peninsula. The number is a review-scale approximation, not a measured reference streamline or dated footprint.

The opening sentence of EGU2009-12242 reports 2,000 km for the northward Malvinas loop of the northern Antarctic Circumpolar Current branch in the Argentine Basin. This is a 2009 conference abstract approximation, not a peer-reviewed reference-path measurement. It supplies no endpoint coordinates, layer-specific length or error interval. The 2009 related journal paper explains the flow and retroflection but is not cited as a source for this number. Keep the return-current extent and Patagonian shelf-break front separate.
